lessons.title: Welcome — Video Advertising
lessons.content:
Welcome to Week 9 of Module 5!

So far, you have learned how to edit different types of videos, create engaging visual experiences, use sound effectively, apply colour grading, and tell stories through video. In this lesson, we are taking those skills into the world of marketing and business.

Today, we will be learning about Video Advertising and how to edit videos that do more than just look attractive. A good advertisement should capture attention, communicate value, influence decisions, and encourage viewers to take action.

Video advertising is the use of video content to promote a product, service, brand, event, or business. You see it every day on platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, and other digital platforms.

As a video editor, understanding advertising is important because businesses and content creators need videos that can attract potential customers and communicate their messages effectively. Your job is not simply to arrange clips and add effects; it is to use editing techniques to help an advertisement achieve its purpose.

Let's explore the key elements that make an advertisement effective.

lessons.title: 1 — What Makes an Advertisement Work?
lessons.content:
A successful advertisement is not necessarily the one with the most effects, transitions, or complicated editing. It is the one that communicates its message clearly and persuades the intended audience to respond.

An effective video advertisement should:

- Capture attention quickly.
- Communicate a clear message.
- Identify a need or problem the audience can relate to.
- Present a product or service as a valuable solution.
- Show why the product or service is worth considering.
- Encourage viewers to take a specific action.

Every part of the advertisement should serve a purpose. The visuals, audio, text, pacing, and overall structure should work together to communicate the message.

lessons.title: 2 — Understanding the Objective of an Ad
lessons.content:
Before editing an advertisement, you need to understand what the advertisement is expected to achieve.

This is called the advertising objective.

Different advertisements have different goals. For example, an advertisement may be designed to:

- Introduce a new product or service.
- Increase awareness of a brand.
- Generate sales or purchases.
- Encourage people to register for an event.
- Get viewers to visit a website.
- Generate enquiries or customer leads.
- Promote a special offer or discount.

As an editor, the objective should influence your editing decisions.

For example, an advertisement promoting a new restaurant may focus on attractive food shots, while an advertisement for an online training programme may focus on the benefits of the programme, testimonials, and a registration call-to-action.

Always understand the goal before you begin editing. This helps you create a video that communicates the right message.

lessons.title: 3 — The Hook: Capturing Attention
lessons.content:
The hook is the opening part of an advertisement that immediately captures the viewer's attention.

On social media, people scroll through content quickly. If your advertisement does not give them a reason to stop, they may simply move on to the next video.

Your opening should therefore create curiosity, highlight an interesting benefit, ask a relevant question, or introduce a problem that your target audience understands.

Some examples include:

- "Struggling to grow your business online?"
- "Here is a better way to organise your daily tasks."
- "Looking for comfortable shoes that match every outfit?"
- Showing an impressive transformation or product result immediately.

As an editor, you can strengthen a hook through:

- Interesting opening shots.
- Well-timed text.
- Strong visual composition.
- Appropriate sound effects.
- Quick cuts and engaging pacing.
- Clear and attention-grabbing captions.

The goal is to make viewers interested enough to continue watching.

lessons.title: 4 — The Problem: Identifying the Audience's Need
lessons.content:
After capturing attention, an advertisement can introduce a problem that the target audience experiences.

This is important because people are more likely to pay attention to a product or service when they understand how it relates to their needs.

For example:

- A skincare advertisement may highlight concerns about dry skin.
- A food delivery advertisement may address the difficulty of finding time to cook.
- A business software advertisement may highlight the challenge of managing tasks manually.

The problem should be relevant to the people the advertisement is targeting.

From an editing perspective, you can communicate a problem through facial expressions, relevant footage, text overlays, voiceovers, and carefully selected B-roll.

The audience should be able to recognise the situation being presented.

lessons.title: 5 — The Solution: Showing How the Product or Service Helps
lessons.content:
Once the problem has been introduced, the advertisement should present a solution.

This is where the product or service becomes important.

The solution should explain how the advertised product or service addresses the problem and why the audience should consider it.

For example, if an advertisement introduces the problem of poor time management, it could present a productivity application as a tool that helps users organise their schedules.

The editing should make this transition clear. You can use a change in visuals, a demonstration, an animated text overlay, or a transition from the problem to the solution.

Avoid making the solution confusing or unnecessarily complicated. The audience should quickly understand the value being offered.

lessons.title: 6 — Product/Service Presentation
lessons.content:
This is the part of the advertisement where the product or service is properly introduced and presented to the audience.

The presentation should make the product or service look appealing while clearly communicating its features and benefits.

As a video editor, you should pay attention to:

- Product shots: Use clear and attractive footage that shows the product properly.
- Close-up shots: Highlight important details, features, or textures.
- Demonstrations: Show how the product works or how the service is delivered.
- Benefits: Use text or voiceovers to communicate what the audience gains.
- Brand identity: Include relevant brand colours, logos, and visual elements.
- Testimonials: Where available and appropriate, include genuine customer experiences.

For example, when editing an advertisement for a clothing brand, you could use shots showing the clothing from different angles, someone wearing the outfit, close-ups of the material, and text highlighting important product details.

Your editing should help the audience understand what is being offered and why it is valuable.

lessons.title: 7 — CTA: Call to Action
lessons.content:
CTA stands for Call to Action.

It is the part of an advertisement that tells viewers what they should do after watching the video.

An advertisement should not leave viewers wondering what their next step should be. If you want them to purchase a product, register for a programme, visit a website, or contact a business, communicate that instruction clearly.

Examples of CTAs include:

- Shop Now.
- Register Today.
- Book Your Appointment.
- Send Us a Message.
- Visit Our Website.
- Order Now.
- Learn More.
- Sign Up Today.

As an editor, you should make the CTA noticeable through clear text, appropriate placement, readable typography, and enough screen time for viewers to understand it.

The CTA should also match the objective of the advertisement. If the goal is to generate registrations, for example, the CTA should encourage viewers to register rather than simply asking them to follow the brand.

lessons.title: 8 — Visual Hierarchy
lessons.content:
Visual hierarchy refers to how visual elements are arranged to guide the viewer's attention and show which information is most important.

In an advertisement, not every element should compete for attention at the same time.

The viewer should be able to identify the most important information quickly, such as:

- The product or service.
- The main benefit or selling point.
- The brand name or logo.
- The price or special offer, where relevant.
- The call to action.

You can establish visual hierarchy through:

- Text size: Important messages should generally be more prominent than supporting information.
- Colour: Use contrasting colours to make important elements stand out.
- Positioning: Place important text and visuals where viewers can easily notice them.
- Spacing: Avoid overcrowding the screen with too many elements.
- Typography: Choose clear, readable fonts and maintain consistency.
- Timing: Give important messages enough time on screen to be understood.

When editing in CapCut Mobile, pay attention to how text, product footage, logos, and other graphics appear together. Make sure the screen does not become cluttered.

Good visual hierarchy makes an advertisement easier to understand and more professional.

lessons.title: 9 — Editing for Conversion
lessons.content:
Editing for conversion means making editing decisions that encourage viewers to take the action the advertisement is designed to achieve.

A conversion could mean a purchase, registration, booking, enquiry, website visit, or another desired action.

This means your editing should not focus only on making the video beautiful. It should also help move the viewer towards the intended result.

Some important considerations include:

- Clear messaging: Make sure viewers understand what is being advertised and what benefit it offers.
- Strong pacing: Keep the video engaging and remove unnecessary sections that may cause viewers to lose interest.
- Relevant visuals: Use footage that supports the message instead of adding random clips simply for decoration.
- Readable text: Ensure that important information is easy to read, especially on mobile screens.
- Product visibility: Give the product or service enough attention so viewers can understand what is being offered.
- Effective audio: Use clear voiceovers, suitable background music, and sound effects that support the advertisement without distracting from the message.
- Strong CTA: Make the next step obvious and easy to understand.

Remember that effective advertising is about communication and persuasion. Every cut, transition, sound effect, text overlay, and visual choice should contribute to the advertisement's objective.

lessons.title: Lesson Goal
lessons.content:
By the end of this lesson, you should understand how video advertisements are structured and what makes them effective.

You should be able to identify the objective of an advertisement, create a strong hook, present a problem and solution, showcase a product or service, establish visual hierarchy, and use editing techniques that encourage viewers to take action.

lessons.title: Closing
lessons.content:
A good video editor knows how to make a video look appealing. A great video editor also understands how to make that video achieve a purpose.

As you continue developing your editing skills, remember that businesses do not just need attractive videos; they need videos that communicate value and help them reach their goals.

Keep learning, pay attention to the details, and approach every advertisement with a clear objective in mind.

lessons.title: Tuesday — Practical Video Advertising
lessons.content:
Welcome to Tuesday's practical lesson!

In our previous lesson, we explored the key elements that make an advertisement effective, including the hook, problem, solution, product presentation, call to action, visual hierarchy, and editing for conversion.

Today, we are moving from understanding these concepts to exploring how they are applied when editing different types of video advertisements.

Not every advertisement is created in the same way. A video promoting a physical product may require a different editing approach from one advertising a professional service. Similarly, an advertisement featuring a content creator speaking directly to the camera may have a different structure from a fast-paced social media product advert.

As a video editor, you need to understand these different advertising formats and know how to adapt your editing style to suit the message, audience, brand, and platform.

Let's explore the different types of advertisements you should know how to edit.

lessons.title: 1 — Product Videos
lessons.content:
Product videos are advertisements created to showcase physical or digital products and encourage people to purchase them.

The purpose is to help viewers understand what the product looks like, what it does, and why they might want or need it.

Examples include advertisements for:

- Clothing and fashion items.
- Skincare and beauty products.
- Electronics and gadgets.
- Food and beverages.
- Shoes, bags, and accessories.
- Digital products such as e-books and online courses.

When editing product videos, pay attention to:

- Product visibility: Make sure the product is clearly shown.
- Close-up shots: Highlight important details, textures, features, and quality.
- Product demonstrations: Show how the product works or how it can be used.
- Text overlays: Highlight important features, benefits, prices, or offers.
- Music and sound effects: Use appropriate audio to make the advertisement engaging.
- Pacing: Arrange clips in a way that maintains interest without rushing important details.

For example, when editing an advertisement for a perfume, you could begin with an attractive opening shot, show close-ups of the bottle, include footage of someone using the perfume, and finish with the product name and a clear call to action.

The goal is to present the product in a way that makes its value easy to understand.

lessons.title: 2 — Service Advertisements
lessons.content:
Unlike product videos, service advertisements promote something a business or professional does rather than a physical item that customers purchase.

Examples include:

- Photography and videography services.
- Cleaning services.
- Digital marketing services.
- Hairdressing and beauty services.
- Consultancy and coaching.
- Catering services.
- Professional training programmes.

When editing service advertisements, your focus should be on communicating the value of the service and building confidence in the business or professional offering it.

You can use:

- Footage showing the service being performed.
- Before-and-after comparisons, where appropriate.
- Customer testimonials and reviews.
- Text overlays explaining the services offered.
- Clips showing the people behind the business.
- Brand logos and contact information.
- A clear call to action encouraging viewers to make enquiries or book.

For example, an advertisement for a photography business could show behind-the-scenes footage of a photoshoot, examples of completed photographs, and a final message inviting viewers to book a session.

The audience should finish watching with a clear understanding of what the business offers and how to access the service.

lessons.title: 3 — UGC-Style Advertisements
lessons.content:
UGC stands for User-Generated Content.

UGC-style advertisements are promotional videos designed to look and feel like natural content created by everyday users or customers rather than traditional, highly polished commercials.

They often feature someone speaking about a product, demonstrating how they use it, sharing an experience, or explaining why they recommend it.

For example, someone might record themselves talking about a skincare product, showing how they use it, and explaining their experience with it.

When editing UGC-style advertisements, focus on:

- Natural-looking cuts and transitions.
- Removing unnecessary pauses and mistakes.
- Adding readable captions or subtitles.
- Including relevant product footage or B-roll.
- Highlighting important statements.
- Keeping the presentation conversational.
- Maintaining a natural and relatable editing style.

Avoid overloading this type of advertisement with too many effects or transitions. The aim is to preserve the authentic, personal feel that makes UGC-style content relatable.

Important: When creating or editing UGC-style advertisements, do not present fabricated customer experiences, testimonials, or product results as genuine. Promotional claims should be truthful and supported.

lessons.title: 4 — Talking-Head Advertisements
lessons.content:
Talking-head advertisements are videos in which a person speaks directly to the camera to promote a product, service, brand, or offer.

The person may be a business owner, brand representative, professional, influencer, or presenter.

For example, a business owner might appear on camera explaining the benefits of a service and inviting viewers to make an enquiry.

As an editor, your responsibility is to make the presentation clear, engaging, and professional.

Important editing techniques include:

- Removing unnecessary pauses: Cut out long silences and irrelevant sections.
- Using jump cuts: Maintain a smooth flow while removing unwanted gaps.
- Adding captions: Make spoken information easier to follow.
- Using punch-ins: Apply subtle zooms to emphasise important statements.
- Adding B-roll: Insert relevant footage to support what the speaker is discussing.
- Balancing audio: Ensure the speaker's voice is clear and audible.
- Highlighting key points: Use text overlays to draw attention to important information.

A talking-head advertisement should not feel unnecessarily long or difficult to follow. Keep the message focused and make sure the viewer understands the offer and the next step.

lessons.title: 5 — Social Media Advertisements
lessons.content:
Social media advertisements are promotional videos created specifically for platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and YouTube.

These advertisements are designed to communicate a message in an environment where viewers are constantly scrolling through content.

Because of this, social media advertisements often need to capture attention quickly, communicate their message clearly, and encourage immediate engagement or action.

When editing social media ads, consider the following:

- Strong opening: Capture attention within the first few seconds.
- Mobile-friendly visuals: Ensure that text and important visual elements are easy to see on smaller screens.
- Captions: Include readable subtitles, especially when people are speaking.
- Engaging pacing: Remove unnecessary sections and maintain the viewer's interest.
- Clear messaging: Avoid presenting too much information at once.
- Brand consistency: Use appropriate brand colours, fonts, and logos.
- Call to action: Make the next step clear.

You should also understand the platform's content style and audience expectations. An advertisement created for TikTok may require a different presentation from one designed for a YouTube placement or Facebook feed.

The goal is to make the advertisement feel appropriate for the platform while still achieving its marketing objective.

lessons.title: 6 — Creating Multiple Ad Variations
lessons.content:
Sometimes, a business does not need just one version of an advertisement. It may need several variations of the same advert to test different approaches or reach different audiences.

This is known as creating ad variations.

For example, a business promoting a skincare product may want:

- One version that begins with a question.
- Another version that begins by showing the product.
- A version that focuses on the product's benefits.
- A version featuring a customer testimonial.
- A shorter version for a different advertising placement.

As an editor, you should be able to create these different versions without having to rebuild the entire project every time.

You can achieve this by:

- Keeping the original project organised.
- Duplicating the project before making major changes.
- Replacing opening hooks.
- Changing text overlays and headlines.
- Adjusting the video length.
- Using different footage or music where appropriate.
- Testing different calls to action.

For example, you could create three versions of the same advertisement, each with a different opening hook but the same main product presentation.

This allows a business to compare different creative approaches and identify which version performs best.

lessons.title: 7 — Editing for Different Platforms
lessons.content:
One important skill in video advertising is knowing how to adapt an advertisement for different platforms.

A video created for one platform may not automatically work well on another because platforms have different video formats, placements, audience behaviours, and content requirements.

As a video editor, you should understand how to adjust your project to suit the intended destination.

Consider the following:

TIKTOK AND INSTAGRAM REELS

These platforms commonly use vertical videos. Advertisements should be engaging, mobile-friendly, and designed to capture attention quickly.

INSTAGRAM AND FACEBOOK FEED

Feed advertisements may appear in different placements and aspect ratios. Ensure that your video is properly framed and that important text and visuals remain visible.

YOUTUBE

YouTube advertisements can appear in different formats, including skippable and non-skippable placements. The opening, pacing, and message should be appropriate for the particular ad format.

GENERAL PLATFORM EDITING CONSIDERATIONS

When adapting videos for different platforms, pay attention to:

- Aspect ratio: Choose the appropriate video dimensions for the placement.
- Resolution: Export at a suitable resolution to maintain visual quality.
- Safe areas: Keep important text, logos, and product details away from areas that may be covered by platform interface elements.
- Captions: Make spoken content accessible and easy to follow.
- Duration: Adjust the video length to suit the intended placement.
- File format: Use an export format supported by the platform.
- Visual presentation: Ensure the video looks good on the devices your audience is likely to use.

In CapCut Mobile, you can use the format or canvas settings to adjust your video's aspect ratio and reposition elements where necessary.

Remember that adapting an advertisement for another platform is not simply about changing its dimensions. You may also need to adjust its pacing, text placement, opening, and overall presentation.

lessons.title: Lesson Goal
lessons.content:
By the end of this practical lesson, you should understand how to approach editing different types of video advertisements, including product videos, service advertisements, UGC-style ads, talking-head ads, and social media ads.

You should also understand how to create multiple ad variations and adapt videos for different platforms while maintaining clear messaging, good visual presentation, and an effective call to action.

lessons.title: Closing
lessons.content:
As a video editor, you should be able to adapt your skills to different clients, businesses, products, services, and advertising needs.

The more familiar you become with different advertising formats, the more confident you will be when handling real-world editing projects.

Keep practising, pay attention to how advertisements communicate their messages, and remember that every editing decision should help the video achieve its purpose.
